chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said:

I asked him about what the trained hunting dog catches for you, and this is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'What you have taught of the hunting beasts, teaching them from what Allah has taught you, so eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of Allah over it.'
He said: There is no harm in you eating from what the dog catches, provided the dog has not eaten from it. If the dog eats from it before you catch it, then do not eat from it.
I also asked him about the catch of the cheetah (fahd) when it is trained for hunting. He said: If you catch it alive, slaughter it and eat it; if it kills it, do not eat from it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game caught by a trained hunting dog if the dog eats from it first?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Sam‘ah ibn Mihran elucidates the conditions for consuming game caught by trained predators, distinguishing between mere capture and actual consumption by the animal. The ruling hinges on whether the dog or cheetah has eaten from the prey before the owner arrives, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the animal's training and the owner's recitation of God's name as prerequisites for permissibility. This specific nuance highlights the practical application of Quranic verses on hunting within the framework of *fiqh*.
